description:
Implement a GitHub Archive benchmark using the GH Archive dataset, which records
the public GitHub timeline since 2011. This benchmark provides a realistic
event-driven analytics workload with nested JSON structures, enabling performance
testing of aggregations, trend analysis, and semi-structured data processing.

GitHub Archive is excellent for benchmarking because:
- Massive scale: 7.5+ billion events, continuously growing
- Real developer activity with natural distributions
- Event-driven schema with nested JSON payloads
- Multiple access methods (BigQuery, ClickHouse, direct download)
- Rich analytical patterns: trending repos, developer metrics, language trends

Use cases covered:
- Repository trending and popularity analysis
- Developer activity and contribution metrics
- Programming language ecosystem trends
- Open source project health metrics
- Event-based time-series analysis

anti_patterns.dont: download from gharchive.org in unit tests
anti_patterns.why: the service rate-limits and files are 50MB+ per hour
the schema is incompatible with post-2015 and adds complexity with no benefit

preserves.behavior: Existing ClickBench JSON handling patterns unchanged

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "from benchbox.core.github_archive import GitHubArchiveBenchmark; print('OK')"

- Events table with JSON payload column
- OR flattened table with sparse columns per event type
- Consider ClickHouse approach (flattened for performance)

Options:
A) Keep payload as JSON, extract at query time
B) Pre-extract common fields into separate columns
C) Create separate tables per event type

Trade-offs: A is flexible but slower, B/C are faster but more complex

GitHub Archive changed schema in March 2015:
- Pre-2015: Timeline API format (different event structure)
- Post-2015: Events API format (current structure)

Options:
A) Only support post-2015 data (simpler, recommended for MVP)
B) Create schema adapter for pre-2015 events
C) Document limitation and allow future extension

Recommendation: Option A for initial implementation, document
pre-2015 as out-of-scope with future enhancement path
